publications.abstract: We present followup observations of the fast evolving, blue and luminous transient SN 2026wpd. The light curve shows a rapid rise to an absolute magnitude of ~ -19 in ~6 days. The LT spectrum displays prominent C III 5696 emission, similar to the transitional Ibn/Icn event SN 2023xgo. The transient is still rising and remains blue, with a hot photospheric temperature. Followup observations are encouraged.
publications.authors_text: S. Srivastav and S. J. Smartt (Oxford)
publications.title: Flash ionisation features in the rapidly evolving transient SN2026wpd

publications.abstract: Here we report the ATLAS discovery of the transient ATLAS26jiy (AT2026wpd) in galaxy CGCG 537-004 at magnitude m_o = 18.26 +/- 0.16. At a distance of 100 Mpc, the transient was discovered on MJD = 61253.50 (2026-08-01.50) with an absolute magnitude of M = -16.9 +/- 0.2. The last non-detection through forced photometry was on MJD = 61251.60. Spectroscopic classification is encouraged.

publications.abstract: We crossmatched all public TNS transients (about 187,000 in the VLASS footprint) with the CIRADA VLASS Quick Look epoch 1 and epoch 2 component catalogs, classifying each radio-coincident transient by the timing of its VLASS subtile observations relative to the optical discovery. A shifted-position control yields about 10 chance matches per epoch against about 2,500 real ones. After archival radio vetting (FIRST/NVSS) and multi-archive characterization (Legacy DR10 host offsets, SDSS spectra, NEOWISE, ZTF light curves), we report 5 unclassified candidates (5 emergent, 0 fading) whose nuclear 3 GHz radio state changed within a window containing the optical event. The method blindly recovers both AT 2020aboe (AstroNote 2026-209) and the published repeating partial TDE AT 2020vdq as its top-ranked known objects. Spectroscopic and radio follow-up of the candidates is encouraged; all data products are available on request.
